problem.text: The existing TransformerBlock feeds its attention-updated residual into the MLP path. This change adds a separate block whose attention and MLP consume the same normalized input.

reasoning.text: Keeping ParallelDecoderBlock separate preserves the sequential block's computation while offering shared-input branch composition. “Parallel” describes data dependencies here: the Python implementation calls attention and then MLP, without introducing concurrent scheduling.

impact.text: ParallelDecoderBlock becomes importable from exllamav3.modules. The diff adds no architecture registration or model construction site; it also broadens TransformerBlock.mlp_norm's annotation to include LayerNorm without changing that block's forward implementation.

source_notes.text: The immediate ancestor entry describes the preceding addition of the exported LayerNorm component, without model-constructor integration.

The inspected discussions report “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” “`cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B` generates incoherent output for bpw <= 2.5,” and “Build Failure on Windows: CUDA 12.4 / PyTorch 2.7.0+cu126 / VS 2022.” Their framing is extension loading, quantization quality, and compilation respectively; none identifies this parallel decoder addition as a remedy.

limitations: No repository implementation, PyTorch operation, GPU kernel, or model integration test was executed.
The scalar check models branch dependencies with integer arithmetic and artificial functions; it does not establish tensor aliasing, half-precision rounding, numerical accuracy, or performance.
Whole-parent-tree searches found no named ParallelDecoderBlock callers; external or dynamically assembled consumers are not established.

claims.text: forward computes y = input_norm(x), requesting torch.half, then adds Attention(y) and MLP(y) into x in place. The MLP receives y rather than the attention-updated residual. There are no separate branch normalizers or post-normalizers in the new block.

A scalar transcription with x=5, N(x)=2x, A(y)=y+1 and M(y)=3y returned 46, matching x+A(N(x))+M(N(x)); feeding the attention-updated residual through normalization into the MLP instead produced 112. The prefill transcription returned 16 after only the attention residual addition.

A truthy params['prefill'] skips the MLP and final dtype conversion, but only after adding attention's output. Model.prefill sets this flag only at the last cache-affecting module and then stops, rather than setting it throughout prompt ingestion. The old TransformerBlock returns before its attention residual addition.
On the ordinary return path, to2 gives the forward-call dtype precedence over the constructor dtype, leaving x unchanged when neither is supplied.

Registering the normalizer, attention and MLP connects them to Module's recursive traversal, loading, unloading and weight counting. num_slices is copied from the MLP, or defaults to one. The block-level qmap argument is not forwarded: the base constructor receives None.

allocate_q follows TransformerBlock's allocation interface: it forwards the selected bit budget, surplus, attention projections and MLP projection collections to allocate_transformer. Conversion calls allocate_q for each model module before loading and calibration. This is reuse of existing allocation machinery, not a new quantization algorithm.

findings.description: The constructor permits omitted components, but forward unconditionally dereferences them; even a block named '(no-op)' cannot execute as an identity.
findings.trigger: Construct ParallelDecoderBlock with input_norm=None, or omit attention or the MLP and reach its corresponding forward call.
findings.expected_behavior: Either reject missing required components during construction or implement the advertised optional/no-op composition.
findings.actual_behavior: forward calls .forward on None. With all defaults, failure occurs at self.input_norm.forward before any residual computation.

verification.description: Compared optional constructor defaults and get_name's no-op label with unconditional forward calls. Whole-parent-tree search found no named users; Model.forward and Model.prefill are generic dispatch sites only if this block is installed.
verification.limits: No concrete integrated model or runtime failure was tested.

findings.description: The new block copies an existing allocation mismatch for the explicitly accepted plain MLP type.
findings.trigger: Call ParallelDecoderBlock.allocate_q with a plain MLP and a valid quantization budget.
findings.expected_behavior: Allocate bits for the plain MLP's up and down projections.
findings.actual_behavior: Argument evaluation accesses self.mlp.ups and self.mlp.downs, whereas MLP defines singular up and down attributes, so allocation cannot reach allocate_transformer successfully.

verification.description: Compared MLP attributes with both block allocators. Whole-parent-tree caller search located conversion's generic module.allocate_q call, which runs before calibration; no named ParallelDecoderBlock construction was found. GatedMLP does define the plural collections and is outside this trigger.
verification.limits: Source-level conditional reach only; conversion was not executed.

annotation.summary: Adds an exported shared-normalization parallel decoder block, without architecture wiring, while retaining optional-component and plain-MLP allocation inconsistencies.

argv:
def parallel(x, prefill=False):
 y=x*2
 y1=y+1
 x+=y1
 if prefill:return x
 y2=y*3
 x+=y2
 return x
x=5
print({'shared_input_result':parallel(x),'formula':x+(2*x+1)+3*(2*x),'prefill_result':parallel(x,True),'sequential_branch_result':x+(2*x+1)+3*(2*(x+(2*x+1)))})
